title: Blue marble - NASA Science
snippet: NASA's Visible Earth catalog entry for the Blue Marble image.
quote: Using a collection of satellite-based observations, scientists and visualizers stitched together months of observations of the land surface, oceans, sea ice, and clouds into a seamless, true-color mosaic of every square kilometer (0.4 square miles) of our planet.
stance_why: NASA itself describes the iconic Blue Marble as a stitched mosaic, supporting the skeptic's point that it is a constructed composite rather than a single photograph.

title: Why Is Our Skyline Visible From Across the Lake? - Chicago Magazine
snippet: Chicago Magazine piece on seeing the skyline across Lake Michigan via looming.
quote: Turns out I wasn't — not directly, anyway. I was looking at the result of an optical phenomenon called atmospheric refraction, or 'looming,' which is 'the appearance of distant objects that are usually hidden by the convexity of the earth\u2019s surface,' according to Andrew Young, a professor of astronomy at San Diego State University.
stance_why: Mainstream source concedes the long-distance sighting is real while invoking a post-hoc refraction mechanism, supporting the skeptic's anomaly-absorption pattern.

title: Long distance observations - Wikipedia
snippet: Wikipedia survey of long-distance observation records.
quote: The longest distance observation ever has been made on December 15, 2024, from a subpeak near Karag\u00f6l summit, Turkey, toward Shkhara on the Georgia\u2013Russia border at a distance of 493 km. It was photographed by Richard Jezik.
stance_why: Documents a photographed 493 km line of sight, supporting the skeptic's point that extreme long-distance observations are routine and routinely patched by refraction.
